title: OwlDocs editor.v1 tool manifest
description: Built-in, semantic, revision-checked document tools. The host injects documentId from its active document thread; models cannot supply a document path. Writes require preview and user acceptance. File open/save/export and other desktop system commands remain user actions.

query.description: Length is measured in Unicode code points; result offsets are UTF-16.

blockId.description: Paragraph ID or, for tableCell results, the cell ID.

heightPoints.description: Optional display height, or bounding-box height when widthPoints is also supplied. The rendered figure always keeps its aspect ratio.

widthPoints.description: Optional display width, or bounding-box width when heightPoints is also supplied. The rendered figure always keeps its aspect ratio.

reconstructScene.description: Use only when the user explicitly requests a full redraw/reconstruction. It permits replacing original scene/label IDs and unsupported objects, with a visible loss warning. Prefer native patches for partial edits.

oneOf.description: Insert a bounded rectangular table at a body paragraph position. Optional tableId and rectangular cellIds let later operations in the same preview address the new table/cells.
Replace one UTF-16 range in a stable table cell, retaining unrelated content and formatting.
Replace the text of one stable cell; unrelated cells are retained.
Format a UTF-16 range within one stable cell.
Set supported paragraph alignment, indents, line/paragraph spacing and keep flags in one stable cell.
Set horizontal and vertical positioning of one stable cell.
Apply one of OwlDocs's supported native table styles.
Set point-based column widths and minimum row heights. Empty arrays restore automatic dimensions; row minimum zero is Auto.
Insert one table row or column, retaining stable identities and inheriting an adjacent row/column.
Insert one table row or column, retaining stable identities and inheriting an adjacent row/column.
Delete contiguous table rows or columns, retaining at least one.
Delete contiguous table rows or columns, retaining at least one.
Evenly distribute column widths. For an automatic grid, supply totalWidthPoints from the available page width.
Evenly distribute authored row minima; optional minimumHeightPoints sets their common minimum. Auto rows remain content-growing.
Apply solid/none borders to the whole table or a rectangular selection of stable cell IDs. Shared edges are updated together.
Delete one semantic table.
Insert bounded base64 PNG/JPEG bytes at a body, stable-cell or header/footer story position. No file paths are accepted.
Resize an existing native body, cell or story picture by stable identity.
Set accessible text without changing picture identity or source bytes.
Set supported body picture wrapping. Cell and story pictures remain inline.
Delete one native picture from its containing body, table cell, header or footer.
Set default header/footer text, or one left/center/right region. PAGE and PAGES fields use {PAGE} and {PAGES}; other regions and their pictures retain identity.
Split a body paragraph at a UTF-16 boundary. Optional newParagraphId lets a later operation in the same preview address the new paragraph.
Merge a body paragraph with its immediately following paragraph, preserving supported atoms and formatting.
Move a paragraph, table or TOC before another body block; omitted/null beforeBlockId appends.
Edit an existing citation locator or reference target/format, retaining the field identity. Computed numbering cannot be assigned.
Change an existing caption label or its pictured object while preserving its paragraph and numbering field identities.
Enable or remove a paragraph's manual bibliography role and generated number prefix. Citations continue referring to its stable identity.

Patch existing native element IDs while preserving all unrelated objects, groups, bindings and assets. Width/height apply only to dimension-bearing objects; line/arrow geometry uses points. Text/fontSize target text elements. No creation, deletion or rebinding.

styleId.description: Set a bounded semantic paragraph-style ID, or null to clear it. IDs are additionally limited to 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Recognized built-ins also apply their catalog baseline; unknown IDs retain identity without invented formatting.

tools.description: Read a bounded snapshot of the active document, including explicit selection and table-cell targets returned by search. Academic reads include offset-safe field metadata, plain note stories, caption/source identities and TOC settings. Request includeFormatting when a user asks about or requests formatting. Use the returned revision, stable block identifiers, and UTF-16 offsets when preparing edits.
tools.name: editor_v1_read

tools.description: Search body paragraphs and table cells in deterministic document order. Results contain stable paragraph/cell identifiers, UTF-16 grapheme-aligned offsets, and bounded context without changing the document.
tools.name: editor_v1_search

tools.description: Create an atomic, revision-checked preview of semantic document operations, including text replacement, character formatting with set_text_style (font, size, bold, italic, underline, colors, highlight, superscript/subscript), paragraph formatting with set_paragraph_style (style, alignment, line/paragraph spacing, keep-with-next), insert_equation/replace_equation, plain footnotes/endnotes, numbered captions, manual numeric bibliography entries/citations, heading/caption cross-references, heading TOCs, and page breaks. Use insert_caption and insert_bibliography_entry to create independent paragraphs, and use returned source IDs for insert_citation and target IDs for insert_cross_reference. TOCs include Heading 1–3 by default, configurable through level 9. When the user asks for a diagram, insert_excalidraw_figure and replace_excalidraw_figure create or revise a native editable scene using the bundled offline renderer: new figures and reconstructions use Professional mode with a white canvas; native patches retain source styling and background. When the user asks you to edit or format the document, use this tool instead of only describing the steps. This never commits changes; the user reviews the preview in OwlDocs before it enters the undo stack.
tools.name: editor_v1_preview

tools.description: Discover built-in OwlDocs editing capabilities, exact operation schemas, grouped features, limits, units and examples. Call before planning an edit; the result also reports current document revision and runtime availability. No skill installation or activation is required. All document writes use editor_v1_preview and user acceptance.
tools.name: editor_v1_capabilities
